title: Differential attention (Ye et al. 2024): every head's softmax becomes softmax(q1 k1) - lambda softmax(q2 k2) over two 16-dim halves of its q/k, headwise RMSNorm, on the 115-fable hybrid ALiBi/NoPE Lean incumbent (4,800,384 params)
description: Idea ID: none in the backlog (new mechanism; nearest are P30 'suppressible retrieval' and P35 attention-logit control). Each of the 8 heads in every Peri-LN block splits its 32-dim q and k into two 16-dim maps and attends with softmax(q1 k1) - lambda softmax(q2 k2) over the same values (lambda = exp(lq1.lk1) - exp(lq2.lk2) + lambda_init per block, lambda_init 0.2..0.67 by depth, headwise RMSNorm x (1 - lambda_init)), the DIFF Transformer recipe at matched parameters (+384), with 115's ALiBi/NoPE slope table applied to both maps and the KV cache unchanged (CPU-checked cached vs full forward 7e-7). Expert iteration samples 7+-line proofs, longer than any pretraining sequence, where the four NoPE content-lookup heads face more distractor keys and softmax spreads mass over them (the failure 113/117-fable showed as unparseable, unbound-name chains at round 1); subtracting a second softmax cancels that common-mode mass so premise retrieval stays sharp at unseen lengths, which should give a better-formed round-1 start for the fixed RL to compound. It differs from the other agent's running 117-claude (a learned sink key that lets a head abstain): DIFF cancels noise on the keys that are attended, it does not add an abstain slot.
hypothesis: Softmax attention assigns non-negligible mass to irrelevant keys, and that noise grows with context length; the DIFF Transformer (Ye et al. 2024) showed that a difference of two softmaxes cancels this common-mode noise, sharpening retrieval of the relevant key and improving length-dependent retrieval (needle tasks, in-context learning) at matched parameters. In this task a proof line cites earlier premises by name; at 7+ lines (never seen in pretraining) the content heads have more candidate keys than in training and 113/117-fable's records show the round-1 failure is malformed chains with unbound names, i.e. retrieval that went to the wrong premise. If differential heads keep the cited premise's attention mass concentrated at those lengths, round-1 samples parse and verify more often, expert iteration starts from more solved targets, and the metric rises. The head-wise RMSNorm keeps the differential output's scale stable so Peri-LN's output norm and RL's AdamW see the same activation scale as 115. Risks: 16-dim per-map q/k halves the resolution of each map at this tiny width; lambda is learned from 300 s of pretraining so it may not settle; two SDPA calls per block cost pretraining steps in a launch-bound model.
expected_delta: -50 to +50 dev solves >= 7 vs 115-fable's 631.33 (central +10); round-1 targets solved 620-800 (115: 718/756/691), round-1 parse failures 12-30% (115: 25/22/18%); pretraining steps 3,300-3,900 (115: 4204/4218/4263; -8% to -22% from the second float-mask SDPA per block plus the head norm), final val loss 0.078-0.088 (115: 0.0826/~0.08); learned lambda ending within 0.1-0.9 in every block (init 0.2..0.67); RL sampling within 20% of 115's 256-313 samples/s (two SDPA calls per block per decode step); totals 1,500-1,900 s under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input), hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads (unchanged from 115) and CHANGED differential attention (Ye et al. 2024, DIFF Transformer) in every head
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope, byte-identical slope table to 115: no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 and 0 for heads 5..8 (NoPE); -inf for masked/future keys. CHANGED: both softmax maps of a head receive that head's bias, so the differential map keeps the head's positional prior
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: attention only. Each head's 32-dim q and k (from the unchanged qkv Linear(256, 768)) are split into two 16-dim halves; the head's attention becomes softmax(q1 k1^T / 4 + bias_h) - lambda * softmax(q2 k2^T / 4 + bias_h) applied to the head's unchanged 32-dim values (two SDPA calls on the same v and attn_mask), followed by a headwise RMSNorm over the 32-dim head output (no affine, eps 1e-6, fp32 statistics) scaled by (1 - lambda_init), then the unchanged proj. lambda = exp(lq1 . lk1) - exp(lq2 . lk2) + lambda_init per block with four learnable 16-dim vectors (one (64,) parameter per block, init N(0, 0.1^2)), lambda_init = 0.8 - 0.6 exp(-0.3 l) for 0-indexed block l = 0.200, 0.356, 0.471, 0.556, 0.619, 0.666. Implemented as DiffAttnBlock(PeriLNBlock) overriding attn(); the fork's KV cache stores k/v in their original (B, 8, max, 32) layout and the halves are split after retrieval. Head count, d_ff, depth, Peri-LN, ALiBiGPT bias build, init of every existing matrix, optimizer, schedule, batch and data are byte-identical to 115. Per-map q/k dimension is 16 instead of 32 (same total q/k width), which is the parameter-matched form of the paper's recipe
arch.n_params_detail: 115's 4,800,000 (vocab 107) + 6 blocks x 64 lambda parameters = 4,800,384; slopes buffer is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py, replace blocks with DiffAttnBlock(256, 8, i) for i in 0..5 as in pretrain.py, then load state (115's keys plus blocks.i.lam). Loading these weights into 115's PeriLNBlock gives a different function (single softmax over the full 32-dim q/k). The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval; the differential maps and lambda persist into RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: same k/v cache tensors and caches[0] key positions as 115; CPU check with the fork's model.py (pinned checkout, lean_tok/make_tokenizer stubbed since the local checkout predates the Lean tokenizer): 3-sequence left-padded prefill of 12 tokens plus 6 cached one-token steps vs the full forward, max abs logit diff 7.2e-7; training forward/backward run with nonzero gradients on every block's lambda; 4,778,368 params at vocab 64 = 4,800,384 at vocab 107

diff_attention.lambda: exp(lq1.lk1) - exp(lq2.lk2) + lambda_init, one scalar per block shared by its 8 heads
diff_attention.lambda_params: (64,) per block = lq1, lk1, lq2, lk2 of dim 16, init normal std 0.1 from the global torch RNG after model construction
diff_attention.head_norm: RMSNorm over each head's 32-dim output, no affine, eps 1e-6, output scaled by (1 - lambda_init)
diff_attention.cost: two float-mask SDPA calls per block per forward instead of one, plus one rsqrt-normalization; CPU fwd+bwd at B16 T160 took 1.85x the 115 block, GPU share expected much smaller

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm; CHANGED: + blocks.i.lam (64 params per block, ndim 1) in the same AdamW group (lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, betas 0.9/0.95); they are excluded from Muon and from the orthogonal init because both select ndim == 2
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1; CHANGED: lambda vectors N(0, 0.1^2) as in the DIFF Transformer reference implementation
